documents.unit: Office of the Provost / Center for Teaching Innovation (CU Committee on Generative AI in Education)
documents.title: CU Committee Report: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Education and Pedagogy
documents.summary: The 2023 committee report from Cornell's provost-convened group sets out why instructors should rethink learning outcomes for generative AI and recommends that each instructor choose among prohibiting, allowing with attribution, or encouraging use. It adds disciplinary examples (including programming), privacy and IP cautions, a recommendation against relying on detectors, and recommendations to faculty and administrators.
documents.stance_why: The report proposes 'a flexible framework in which instructors can choose to prohibit, to allow with attribution, or to encourage GAI use', and recommends that the Code give 'individual faculty ... authority to determine when its use is prohibited, attributed, or encouraged'. It sets no single rule, so the stance is delegates with three named options.

units.why: The executive summary sets the report's whole framework: instructors 'can choose to prohibit, to allow with attribution, or to encourage GAI use'. It is a stance-level policy about who decides, so P04 (instructor decides) fits; the named three options are coded separately as P05 below.
units.anchor: instructors can choose to prohibit, to allow with attribution, or to encourage GAI use
units.policy: Instructors can choose to prohibit, to allow with attribution, or to encourage GAI use.

units.why: This sentence states why AI must be considered in course design: 'since these technologies will not only be present in the future workplace, but are already being used by students.' It ties AI decisions to learning objectives, so P83 fits better than P44, which is about teaching AI as a career skill.
units.anchor: Educators must take generative artificial intelligence (GAI) into account when considering the learning objectives
units.policy: Educators must take generative AI into account when considering the learning objectives for their classes.

units.why: The same sentence adds that tools 'may also hide biases, inaccuracies, and ethical problems, including violations of privacy and intellectual property'. This is a naming of harms, so P53.

documents.title: AI & Academic Integrity

ANY-AI-UA (encouraged on identified assignments with attribution)
documents.summary: Cornell's Center for Teaching Innovation guidance for instructors on communicating AI policy, preventing and responding to AI-related integrity concerns, citing AI, and why detectors should not be relied on. It supplies four sample syllabus statements ranging from an AI ban to encouraged use.
documents.stance_why: The page gives instructors four sample statements (AI-FREE, AS-UA, ANY-AI-UA, AS) and says to 'clearly communicate your policies', so the university guidance leaves the stance to each instructor and offers tiers; it does not set one rule.

units.why: CTI tells instructors to 'clearly communicate your policies regarding the use of generative AI in your syllabus, in assignment instructions, and verbally in class'. It sets the place and ways to state expectations, so P09.
units.anchor: clearly communicate your policies regarding the use of generative AI in your syllabus, in assignment

units.why: The page says 'When generative AI is permitted, clarify expectations for documentation and attribution'. Instructors state the disclosure rule, so P24.
units.anchor: When generative AI is permitted, clarify expectations for documentation and attribution
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors, who must clarify documentation and attribution expectations.

units.why: The page says to 'Discuss with students how generative AI output can be incorrect or problematic'. An instruction to talk with students, so P66.
units.anchor: Discuss with students how generative AI output can be incorrect or problematic
units.fit_note: Content is that AI output can be wrong (P31); the action is to discuss it.

units.why: Students 'are responsible for verifying the output and references if AI use is allowed for an assignment'. Verify output, so P31.
